items.name: Dumbbells
items.description: Hand-held weights with a short handle and a fixed load on each end. The most versatile free weight for presses, rows, curls, lunges and carries.
items.weight_options: 1–50+ kg (2–120 lb) pairs, usually in 1–2.5 kg (2.5–5 lb) steps
items.adjustability: Fixed per dumbbell; a full rack covers the range.
items.buying_tips: Rubber or urethane heads protect floors; knurled steel handles grip better than chrome. Buy pairs in the range you will actually use.
items.safety: Set dumbbells down under control rather than dropping them.
items.keywords: db free weights pro style round

items.name: Hex dumbbells
items.description: Fixed dumbbells with six-sided rubber or iron heads that do not roll. Stable on the floor for push-ups, renegade rows and burpee complexes.
items.buying_tips: Rubber-coated hex heads are quieter and floor-friendly; check the head is bonded tightly to the handle.
items.safety: Check heads are tight before putting body weight on them in push-up positions.

items.name: Adjustable dumbbells
items.description: A pair of dumbbells whose load changes with a dial, pin or slide selector while sitting in a cradle. Replaces a whole rack in a small space.
items.weight_options: Typically 2–24 kg (5–52.5 lb) or 2.5–41 kg (5–90 lb) per hand
items.adjustability: Dial, pin, slide or twist selector; 1–2.5 kg steps.
items.buying_tips: Check the minimum and maximum weight, step size, length at light settings and whether it tolerates drops (most do not).
items.safety: Never drop selector dumbbells, and make sure the selector has fully locked before lifting.

items.name: Spin-lock dumbbell handles
items.description: Threaded dumbbell handles you load with small plates and secure with spin-lock collars. A cheap way to build adjustable dumbbells.
items.weight_options: Handle ~2 kg; sets load to 10–30 kg per hand (1-inch or Olympic 2-inch versions)
items.adjustability: Add or remove plates; slow to change.
items.buying_tips: Olympic-diameter handles let you share plates with your barbell; long handles limit some movements.
items.safety: Re-tighten the spin-lock collars every set; loose plates can slide off.

items.name: Kettlebells
items.description: Cast-iron balls with a thick handle, with the weight sitting below the grip. Built for swings, cleans, snatches, goblet squats and carries.
items.buying_tips: Single-piece cast iron with a smooth, seamless handle; check the handle width fits two hands for swings.
items.safety: Swing with your hips, not your lower back, and keep a clear space around you.

items.name: Competition kettlebell
items.description: Steel kettlebells that are the same size at every weight, with a uniform handle for kettlebell sport. Technique stays identical as weight goes up.
items.buying_tips: Pick a 33–35 mm handle for sport; cheaper "pro-grade" bells may not be true competition spec.

items.name: Adjustable kettlebell
items.description: A kettlebell whose weight changes by adding plates or using a dial or pin selector. Saves buying a full set.
items.weight_options: Usually 4–18 kg or 12–32 kg; plate-loadable handles up to ~40 kg
items.buying_tips: Shell size at light settings matters for cleans and snatches; check locking mechanism quality.
items.safety: Confirm the selector or plate lock is secure before swinging.

items.name: Clubbells / Indian clubs
items.description: Long bottle-shaped weights held at the thin end and swung in circles. Train rotational strength, grip and shoulder mobility.
items.buying_tips: Start very light (Indian clubs or 4–7 kg) to learn patterns; check the handle has a knob so it cannot fly out.
items.safety: Swing only in a clear area with plenty of ceiling height.

items.name: Steel mace
items.description: A long steel handle with a weighted ball on one end, swung around the body. Builds rotational strength, grip and shoulder control.
items.buying_tips: A 7 kg mace is plenty to start for most people; length changes leverage more than weight.
items.safety: Needs a lot of overhead and side clearance.

items.name: Dumbbell rack
items.description: Two- or three-tier rack or tree that holds dumbbells or kettlebells off the floor. Keeps weights tidy and easy to grab.
items.buying_tips: Match the saddle width to your dumbbell heads; A-frame trees suit small home sets.

items.name: Olympic barbell
items.description: A 2.2 m, 20 kg steel bar with 50 mm rotating sleeves that take Olympic plates. The base of squats, bench presses, deadlifts and Olympic lifts.
items.weight_options: Bar 20 kg (44 lb), 2.2 m, 28–29 mm shaft; holds 300+ kg
items.buying_tips: A multipurpose 28.5 mm bar with bushings or bearings, dual knurl marks and ~190k PSI tensile strength suits most lifters.
items.safety: Use collars and safeties, and never bench or squat heavy without a spotter or safety arms.

items.name: Women's Olympic bar
items.description: A 15 kg, 2.01 m Olympic bar with a thinner 25 mm shaft for smaller hands. Standard in women's weightlifting and good for any lifter with small hands.
items.buying_tips: Bearing sleeves for Olympic lifts; no centre knurl is typical.

items.name: Technique / training bar
items.description: A light aluminium or steel bar (often 5–10 kg) with full-size sleeves, used for learning lifts and for beginners or youth.
items.buying_tips: Look for a bar that takes 50 mm plates so it can grow with technique and bumper plates. Max load is usually low (~50–100 kg).
items.safety: Respect the low load rating.
items.keywords: technique bar aluminum training youth junior

items.name: Short Olympic bar
items.description: A 1.5–1.8 m bar with Olympic sleeves for small rooms. Fine for floor and bench work but too short for most standard racks.
items.buying_tips: Check it reaches across the uprights of your rack or bench before buying.

items.name: Powerlifting bar
items.description: A stiff 20 kg, 29 mm bar with aggressive knurling and a centre knurl. Built for heavy squats, bench presses and deadlifts with minimal whip.
items.buying_tips: Stiffness and grippy knurl are the point; IPF knurl marks matter for meet prep.

items.name: Deadlift bar
items.description: A longer, thinner (27 mm), whippier 20 kg bar that bends before the plates leave the floor, letting you pull more weight.
items.buying_tips: Only worth it for competitive powerlifters; don't use it for squats or bench.
items.safety: Not rated for squatting or benching.

items.name: Standard 1-inch bar
items.description: A thin, cheap barbell with 25 mm (1-inch) ends that takes standard plates. Common in starter home sets.
items.buying_tips: Fine for light work; upgrade to an Olympic bar once lifts get heavier.
items.safety: The thin bar bends and is not rated for heavy squats or deadlifts.

items.name: Fixed-weight barbells
items.description: Pre-loaded short barbells (straight or EZ) with welded or bolted plates, usually on a rack in commercial gyms. Grab-and-go for curls, extensions and rows.
items.weight_options: 10–50 kg in 2.5–5 kg steps; straight and EZ versions
items.buying_tips: For home, a few fixed EZ bars are a space-saving middle ground.
items.keywords: fixed barbell pro style preloaded straight ez

items.name: EZ curl bar
items.description: A short bar with zig-zag bends that let wrists sit at an angle. Easier on wrists for curls, skull crushers and upright rows.
items.weight_options: 7–12 kg; 1.2–1.3 m; Olympic or standard sleeves
items.buying_tips: Olympic-sleeve EZ bars share plates with your barbell; "super curl" bars have a deeper bend.

items.name: Triceps / hammer bar
items.description: A rectangular bar with two parallel neutral-grip handles inside a frame. Used for hammer curls, neutral-grip extensions and close presses.
items.buying_tips: Olympic sleeves and a 1.5 inch handle are the common spec.
items.keywords: tricep bar hammer curl bar neutral

items.name: Trap / hex bar
items.description: A hexagonal bar you stand inside, with handles at your sides. Makes deadlifts, shrugs and carries easier on the lower back.
items.weight_options: 20–30 kg; most have low and high handles
items.buying_tips: Look for raised (high) handles and 60+ cm inside width; check sleeve length if you lift heavy.
items.keywords: hex bar trap bar diamond shrug bar

items.name: Open trap bar
items.description: A trap bar with one side open, so you can step in and out. Also allows lunges, split squats and longer strides without hitting the frame.
items.adjustability: Dual-height handles; some have rack hooks.
items.buying_tips: More expensive than a closed hex bar; worth it if you want carries and lunges.
items.keywords: open trap bar open hex kabuki rogue tib

items.name: Safety squat bar
items.description: A padded yoke bar with forward handles and cambered ends. Lets you squat with sore shoulders and loads the upper back and quads harder.
items.buying_tips: Check camber, pad comfort and whether it fits your rack's J-cups.
items.safety: Rack it carefully; the pad shifts the balance forward.

items.name: Cambered bar
items.description: A barbell whose ends drop down several inches below the shaft, so the weight swings and sits lower. Used for squats, good mornings and bench press.
items.buying_tips: Rare in home gyms; check drop depth and that it fits your rack.
items.safety: The swinging plates demand control; use safeties.

items.name: Swiss / multi-grip bar
items.description: A barbell frame with several neutral and angled grips. Easier on shoulders and elbows for presses, rows and curls.
items.buying_tips: Angled grips feel better than straight neutral ones for most; check the bar fits your J-cups.
items.keywords: football bar swiss bar multi grip neutral

items.name: Axle bar
items.description: A thick (about 5 cm) bar with no rotating sleeves or knurl, used in strongman. Builds grip and makes deadlifts and cleans much harder to hold.
items.buying_tips: Use with a belt-clean style; check the bar holds Olympic plates without slipping.
items.keywords: axle fat bar thick bar strongman apollon

items.name: Buffalo bar
items.description: A barbell with a gentle curve through the middle that wraps around the back. Easier on the shoulders for back squats and good mornings.
items.buying_tips: Mainly a powerlifting accessory; check it fits your rack.

items.name: Duffalo / bow bar
items.description: A barbell with a deep bow in the centre, letting the hands go lower on bench or wrap around the back on squats.
items.buying_tips: Mainly for powerlifting gyms; the bend gives extra bench range of motion.

items.name: Flexible / tsunami bar
items.description: A bendy bar (composite or bamboo) with plates or kettlebells hung from bands, so the load oscillates. Trains stability for bench, squat and press.
items.weight_options: Bar 2–7 kg; loaded with plates or hung kettlebells
items.adjustability: Hang load from bands for more instability.
items.buying_tips: Bamboo bars with band-hung kettlebells are cheaper; tsunami bars take plates directly.
items.safety: Use light weights; the oscillation makes sudden loss of control possible.
items.keywords: tsunami bamboo earthquake bandbell oscillating flex bar

items.name: Weight plates
items.description: Cast-iron or urethane plates with a 50 mm hole that load Olympic bars, trap bars and plate-loaded machines.
items.buying_tips: Machined cast iron is cheapest per kg; urethane or rubber coated is quieter. Buy pairs.
items.safety: Never drop iron plates from height; they crack floors and plates.

items.name: Tri-grip / handled plates
items.description: Olympic plates with three cut-out hand holes, so they are easier to carry and can be used for plate exercises like front raises and halos.
items.buying_tips: Handled rubber plates double as dumbbell substitutes for many moves.
items.keywords: tri grip handle plate grip plates

items.name: Standard 1-inch plates
items.description: Plates with a 25–28 mm hole for standard bars and spin-lock dumbbell handles. Cheap and common in starter sets.
items.buying_tips: They do not fit Olympic bars; buy Olympic plates if you might upgrade.

items.name: Bumper plates
items.description: Thick rubber plates all the same diameter, made to be dropped from overhead. Essential for Olympic lifting and CrossFit.
items.buying_tips: Low-bounce virgin rubber or urethane lasts longest; 10 kg bumpers are thick, so check bar sleeve space.
items.safety: Drop only on a platform or rubber floor, and not with an empty bar.

items.name: Competition bumper plates
items.description: IWF-spec calibrated bumper plates with steel hubs, thin profile and colour coding. Used in weightlifting meets and serious clubs.
items.buying_tips: Overkill for most home lifters; good training bumpers suffice.

items.name: Technique plates
items.description: Light plastic or rubber plates at full bumper diameter, so a light bar sits at the right height for learning lifts.
items.buying_tips: Pair with a technique bar for beginners and kids.
items.keywords: technique plates training plastic full diameter

items.name: Calibrated steel plates
items.description: Thin, precisely weighed steel plates used in powerlifting meets. Fit more weight on the bar and are accurate to a few grams.
items.buying_tips: Only needed for meet-style heavy training or very heavy lifters running out of sleeve.
items.safety: Do not drop; they are not designed for it.

items.name: Fractional plates
items.description: Small plates (0.25–2.5 kg, or 0.25–1.25 lb microplates) for tiny jumps in weight. Keep progress going on presses and curls.
items.weight_options: Change plates 0.5–2.5 kg; microplates 0.25–1 kg (0.25–1.25 lb); magnetic versions for dumbbells
items.buying_tips: A 0.25–1 kg set is cheap and lets you progress 0.5 kg at a time; magnetic micro-weights also work on dumbbells.
items.keywords: fractional micro change plates small increments

items.name: Barbell collars
items.description: Clips or clamps that hold plates on the bar sleeves. Stop plates sliding off and keep load even.
items.weight_options: Spring clips, lock-jaw/clip collars, screw or lever competition collars (2.5 kg each)
items.buying_tips: Lock-jaw style is quick and reliable; spring clips loosen with wear.
items.safety: Always use collars on moving or overhead lifts.

items.name: Plate tree
items.description: A stand with pegs that holds weight plates, often with bar holders. Keeps plates off the floor and easy to reach.
items.buying_tips: Look for wheels and bar holders; rack-mounted plate horns save floor space.
items.safety: Load evenly to avoid tipping.

items.name: Flat bench
items.description: A padded flat bench at about knee height. The base for bench presses, dumbbell rows, hip thrusts and step-ups.
items.buying_tips: A rock-solid frame and grippy pad matter more than features; 43 cm height and 28–30 cm pad suit most.

items.name: Competition bench
items.description: A heavy flat bench built to IPF spec (42–45 cm high, wide pad) for powerlifting bench press with stable leg drive.
items.buying_tips: Wider 30 cm pad and grippy vinyl help; must fit inside your rack.
items.keywords: competition bench ipf powerlifting wide pad

items.name: High flat / row bench
items.description: A tall flat bench that lets you lie face down and row a barbell or dumbbells without hitting the floor.
items.buying_tips: Plyo boxes or a flat bench on blocks can stand in.
items.safety: Get on and off carefully; it is high and narrow.
items.keywords: seal row bench high bench row bench

items.name: Olympic bench with uprights
items.description: A flat bench with built-in bar uprights (and often spotter catches) for bench pressing without a rack.
items.buying_tips: Look for spotter catches; cheap home versions with leg attachments wobble.
items.safety: Use spotter catches or a spotter; a fixed bench cannot save you from a failed rep.

items.name: Incline bench
items.description: A fixed bench set at about 30–45 degrees, usually with bar uprights. For incline barbell and dumbbell presses.
items.buying_tips: At home an adjustable bench covers this.

items.name: Decline bench
items.description: A bench set head-down at about 15–30 degrees with leg rollers. For decline presses and decline sit-ups.
items.buying_tips: Make sure the leg rollers lock your feet securely.
items.safety: Use a spotter for heavy barbell decline work.

items.name: Adjustable bench
items.description: A bench whose back pad adjusts from flat to upright (flat/incline). The single most useful bench for home gyms.
items.buying_tips: Check the gap between seat and back pad at incline, the ladder angles and weight rating.

items.name: FID bench
items.description: An adjustable bench that goes flat, incline and decline, usually with a leg holder for decline sit-ups and presses.
items.buying_tips: Check stability in decline and that the leg holder doesn't get in the way flat.

items.name: Utility / shoulder press bench
items.description: A short fixed bench with an upright back (near 90 degrees) for seated dumbbell or barbell presses and curls.
items.buying_tips: An adjustable bench usually covers this at home.
items.keywords: utility bench shoulder press seat 90 degree

items.name: Preacher curl bench
items.description: A seat with an angled arm pad that pins the upper arms for strict curls.
items.buying_tips: Some adjustable benches have a preacher attachment.
items.safety: Don't let the bar crash at the bottom; control the stretch.

items.name: Folding bench
items.description: A flat or adjustable bench that folds flat or stands upright for storage. For small homes.
items.buying_tips: Check weight rating and wobble; cheaper ones flex under heavy pressing.

items.name: Hip thrust bench
items.description: A low bench or box with a back pad at the right height for hip thrusts, often with band pegs or a foot plate.
items.buying_tips: A flat bench placed against a wall works almost as well.
items.safety: Brace the bench so it cannot slide back.
items.keywords: hip thrust bench glute box thruster

items.name: Bench leg attachment
items.description: A leg extension and leg curl arm that bolts onto a home bench and takes plates.
items.buying_tips: Check it fits your bench brand; many are model-specific.
items.keywords: leg developer extension curl attachment bench

items.name: Squat rack / power rack
items.description: A four-post cage with adjustable J-hooks and safety bars, letting you squat, bench and press heavy alone.
items.adjustability: Hole spacing for J-cups and safeties.
items.buying_tips: Check ceiling height, depth, hole spacing (Westside spacing near bench height) and attachment ecosystem.
items.safety: Set safety bars just below the bottom of every rep.

items.name: Half rack
items.description: Two uprights with J-cups and short spotter arms, often with a pull-up bar. Takes less depth than a full cage.
items.buying_tips: Spotter arms must be long enough to catch the bar where you bench and squat.
items.safety: Set spotter arms for every heavy set.

items.name: Squat stands
items.description: Two independent or base-linked uprights with J-cups. The cheapest and smallest way to rack a barbell.
items.buying_tips: Base-linked stands are more stable; independent stands need careful spacing.
items.safety: Add spotter arms or straps, or bench and squat with a spotter.

items.name: Folding wall rack
items.description: A wall-mounted rack that swings out for training and folds flat against the wall afterwards. Ideal for garages.
items.buying_tips: Needs solid studs or masonry for mounting; check it folds past your car mirror.
items.safety: Must be bolted into structural framing.
items.keywords: folding rack wall mount garage pr-4100

items.name: Squat / bench combo rack
items.description: A competition-style rack whose hooks adjust for both squats and bench press, with spotter catches and room for a bench.
items.buying_tips: Found in powerlifting gyms and meets.
items.safety: Set spotter catches every time.

items.name: Monolift
items.description: A rack whose hooks swing away after unracking, so you squat without walking the bar out. Used for very heavy powerlifting squats.
items.buying_tips: Rare outside powerlifting gyms.
items.safety: Needs trained operators or spotters.

items.name: Rig
items.description: A long, modular steel frame joining several rack bays, pull-up bars and attachments. Standard in CrossFit and functional gyms.
items.buying_tips: Bolt to the floor or a platform; plan bay widths for barbell work.
items.keywords: rig crossfit functional rig monkey bars

items.name: Spotter arms / safety straps
items.description: Safety bars, pins, arms or nylon straps that catch a failed barbell. Make heavy squats and bench safe alone.
items.buying_tips: Straps are quieter and kinder to bars; flip-down arms suit half racks and stands.
items.safety: Set them every set just below your lowest bar position.
items.keywords: spotter arms safety straps pins safeties

items.name: J-cups / J-hooks
items.description: The hooks that hang on rack uprights to hold the bar. Usually included with a rack; extra pairs or roller versions are common upgrades.
items.buying_tips: Plastic-lined (UHMW) hooks protect bar knurling.
items.safety: Seat both hooks fully before loading.
items.keywords: j hooks j cups rack hooks

items.name: Rack dip attachment
items.description: Dip handles that slot onto a rack upright for dips and knee raises.
items.buying_tips: Y-shaped handles allow different widths.
items.keywords: dip attachment rack dip bars station

items.name: Jammer / lever arms
items.description: Pivoting plate-loaded arms that attach to a rack, turning it into a press, row or squat machine.
items.buying_tips: Check compatibility with your rack's upright size and hole spacing.

items.name: Landmine attachment
items.description: A pivoting sleeve that holds one end of a barbell on the floor or a rack. For angled presses, rows, rotations and squats.
items.buying_tips: A rack-mounted landmine saves floor; a corner and a towel works as a stand-in.

items.name: Landmine handle
items.description: Handles that fit over the end of a landmine barbell: V-grip for T-bar rows or wide Viking press handles.
items.buying_tips: Rubber-coated handles are comfortable; check sleeve diameter.
items.keywords: landmine handle viking press t bar handle

items.name: Lifting platform
items.description: A wood centre with rubber side pads for deadlifts and Olympic lifts. Protects floors and lets you drop bumper plates.
items.buying_tips: A DIY platform of plywood and horse-stall mats is the budget choice.
items.keywords: platform deadlift drop olympic lifting mats

items.name: Pulling blocks
items.description: Stackable foam or wooden blocks that raise the plates to a set height for block pulls and hang-position Olympic lifts.
items.buying_tips: Foam blocks are quieter and safer to drop onto than wood.
items.keywords: blocks pulling blocks block pull deficit

items.name: Jerk blocks
items.description: Paired tall blocks at shoulder height. You jerk from them and can drop the bar back onto them safely.
items.buying_tips: Weightlifting-club equipment.

items.name: Lifting chains
items.description: Heavy chains hung from the bar sleeves so load increases as you lift (more chain leaves the floor at lockout).
items.buying_tips: Lead chains with collars make adjustments easy.
items.safety: Secure the chains so they do not swing off the sleeves.

items.name: Barbell bands & band pegs
items.description: Heavy loop bands anchored to pegs or the rack and looped over the bar ends, to add load at lockout or help (reverse bands) at the bottom.
items.buying_tips: Rack band pegs or a band-peg platform keep bands from slipping.
items.safety: Check bands for nicks; a snapped band whips hard.

items.name: Deadlift jack
items.description: A small lever that lifts a loaded barbell off the floor so plates can slide on and off easily.
items.buying_tips: Mini plate-ramp wedges are a cheaper alternative.
items.keywords: barbell jack deadlift jack plate loading

items.name: Dip belt
items.description: A belt with a chain that hangs plates or a kettlebell from the hips, to add weight to dips, pull-ups and belt squats.
items.buying_tips: Leather or nylon with a long chain; check it can take kettlebells too.
items.keywords: dip belt weighted pull up chain belt

items.name: Lifting belt
items.description: A stiff belt worn around the waist to brace against during heavy squats, deadlifts and presses.
items.weight_options: 10 mm or 13 mm leather; nylon/velcro versions
items.buying_tips: A 10 mm single-prong belt suits most lifters; lever belts are quick but size-locked.
items.safety: A belt helps bracing but does not replace it.
items.keywords: lifting belt weight belt powerlifting lever

items.name: Lifting straps
items.description: Cotton, nylon or leather straps that wrap the bar and your wrist, so grip doesn't limit heavy pulls and rows.
items.buying_tips: Lasso straps are versatile; figure-8 for max pulls; hooks are quick.
items.safety: Don't use figure-8 straps for Olympic lifts; you can't bail.
items.keywords: lifting straps hooks figure 8 versa grips

items.name: Chalk
items.description: Magnesium carbonate (block, loose or liquid) that dries the hands for a better grip on bars and handles.
items.buying_tips: Liquid chalk is less messy and allowed in many gyms that ban loose chalk.

items.name: Wrist wraps
items.description: Elastic wraps with thumb loops that brace the wrist on heavy presses and front-rack positions.
items.buying_tips: 45–60 cm medium stiffness suits most lifters.

items.name: Knee sleeves
items.description: Neoprene sleeves that keep knees warm and add a little support in squats and Olympic lifts.
items.buying_tips: 7 mm stiff sleeves for powerlifting; 5 mm for CrossFit and Olympic lifting.

items.name: Knee wraps
items.description: Long, stiff elastic wraps wound tightly around the knees to store energy and add weight to heavy squats.
items.buying_tips: Only for equipped-style heavy squatting; not for daily training.
items.safety: Wraps cut circulation; remove them between sets.

items.name: Elbow sleeves
items.description: Neoprene sleeves for the elbows that keep joints warm on heavy pressing and triceps work.

items.name: Weightlifting shoes
items.description: Stiff shoes with a raised heel that help squat depth and stability in Olympic lifts and squats.
items.buying_tips: Flat, firm shoes suit low-bar squats and deadlifts better.

items.name: Squat wedge / slant board
items.description: An angled wedge or slant board that raises the heels for deeper, more quad-focused squats and calf stretching.
items.buying_tips: A pair of small plates under the heels works as a stand-in.
items.keywords: slant board squat wedge heel elevation

items.name: Bar pad
items.description: A foam sleeve that wraps a barbell to cushion the hips in hip thrusts and glute bridges.
items.buying_tips: Thick, dense foam is best; avoid using it for squats.
items.safety: Don't use a pad for back squats; it makes the bar roll.
items.keywords: bar pad hip thrust pad manta ray

items.name: Bench press boards
items.description: Stacked boards placed on the chest to shorten the range of motion for board presses and overload lockout.
items.buying_tips: Foam bench blocks with straps (e.g. bench block) are easier to use alone.
items.safety: Use a spotter; boards can shift.

items.name: Slingshot
items.description: Elastic sleeves worn over the elbows that help bench press off the chest so you can handle overload.

items.name: Neck harness
items.description: A head harness with a chain for hanging plates, used to strengthen the neck.
items.buying_tips: Start very light and progress slowly.
items.safety: Neck training must be light and slow; avoid jerking movements.
